Madison-Ridgeland Academy Athletic Director John Weaver announced today that Drew Williams has been named head coach of the Lady Patriot volleyball program and will begin leading the team in the 2027–2028 season.

Williams takes over a Lady Patriot program that has captured three consecutive MAIS state championships, building on a tradition of excellence shaped by dedicated student-athletes, strong leadership, and a commitment to competing at the highest level.

“Lady Patriot volleyball has established a standard of excellence through the dedication of our players, coaches, and families,” said Weaver. “We were looking for a leader who would be on campus full-time and honor that tradition while bringing the knowledge, energy, and vision to build on it. Drew understands the expectations that come with leading this program and shares our commitment to developing young ladies as athletes, teammates, and leaders. We’re excited to welcome him to the Patriot family.”

Williams joins MRA from the University of Southern Mississippi, where he is in his second season as an assistant coach for Southern Miss Volleyball. He was promoted to the role after the 2024 season, following his time as a student coach for the Golden Eagles. Before that, he spent three years as a student assistant and volunteer assistant with the Southern Miss Beach Volleyball program, contributing to the team’s third-place finish at the 2024 Sun Belt Conference Tournament.

"We are so excited for Drew and for the MRA volleyball family. Drew has been a huge part of what we've built at Southern Miss. He brings energy to the gym every day; he connects with players, and he cares about them as people first. He knows the game, he works relentlessly, and he's ready for this. MRA is getting a coach who will hold athletes to a high standard and care about them every day. We'll miss him in our gym, but we couldn't be prouder,” said Southern Miss Volleyball head coach Jenny Hazelwood.

Along with his collegiate experience, Williams brings a strong background in high school and club volleyball. From 2022 to 2024, he served as an assistant coach at Presbyterian Christian School in Hattiesburg, helping develop multiple All-State selections and collegiate signees. He also serves as Assistant Director and head coach for Infinity Volleyball Academy in Hattiesburg.

“Drew is an outstanding up-and-coming coach. His passion for the game combined with his incredible work ethic makes him a home run hire. I’m excited to see the immediate impact Drew has on this program,” said Ray Lewis, assistant coach at the University of Alabama.

A 2022 recipient of the AVCA Thirty Under 30 Award, Williams earned his bachelor’s degree in Sport Management from Southern Miss in 2024 and will complete his master’s degree in Sport Management there in December.

“I’m incredibly excited and grateful for the opportunity to become the Head Volleyball Coach at Madison-Ridgeland Academy! MRA has established an incredible championship tradition, and I’m thankful for the trust placed in me to lead this program,” said Williams. “My focus will be on developing our athletes both on and off the court while building a culture centered around commitment, accountability, and trust. I look forward to getting to know our players and families, building on this program's success, and continuing to compete for championships. I can’t wait to get started and be part of the MRA family!”

REGIONAL SPORTS ROUNDUP
Wednesday, November 11, 2026

COLLEGE

RACERS ROUT BRAVES
Murray State men's basketball improved to 3-0 with a convincing 94-57 victory over Alcorn State last night at the CFSB Center. Roman Domon scored 20 points in the first half and matched his career high with 29, while Brayden Shorter added 19 points with 5 three-pointers. Brigham Rogers contributed 12 rebounds as the Racers built a 21-point halftime lead and cruised to the win. Murray State shot 47 percent from the field and forced 21 turnovers, turning them into 34 points. The Racers return to action Friday night at 7 when they host Texas Southern.

KANSAS ROLLS UK
No. 24 Kentucky suffered its first loss of the season last night, falling 89-69 to No. 15 Kansas in the Champions Classic in Chicago. Zoom Diallo led the Wildcats with 24 points, while Malachi Moreno added a career-high 19. Turnovers proved costly for Kentucky, which committed 15 giveaways that led to 22 Kansas points. The Jayhawks pulled away with a second-half scoring run to drop the Wildcats to 2-1. Kentucky returns home Friday to host Northern Arizona.

CFP RANKINGS UPDATE
The latest College Football Playoff rankings have been released, and Georgia is back to number one.  The Bulldogs are followed by Utah, Alabama, and UCLA.  Notre Dame, Texas, Miami, Tennessee, Indiana, BYU, Kentucky and Texas Tech round out the remainder of the top 12 teams.  Oklahoma State is number 25 after not being included in last week's rankings.

MVC WBB AWARDS
UIC's Julia Coleman is the Missouri Valley Conference Women's Basketball Player of the Week, Illinois State's Hannah Chicken is the Newcomer of the Week, and Belmont freshman Chelby Jordan earned Freshman of the Week honors. 

Coleman averaged 16.3 points, highlighted by a 29-point performance against Northwestern. 

Chicken averaged 16 points and 10.3 rebounds while helping Illinois State open the season 3-0. 

Jordan averaged 15 points, 4.3 rebounds and four assists in her first three collegiate games, including a career-high 20 points against Columbia.

VOLS CBA AGREEMENT
The Tennessee men's basketball team will be the first college sports program in the country with a collective bargaining agreement.  The team released a CBA term sheet today after a series of negotiations with the university's athletic department.  The pending agreement includes a salary cap and floor, and rules governing eligibility and transfers.  Players cut the deal with the help of college sports players association https://t.co/V6OLBSXcEG to show what an agreement between players and schools could look like.

PROS

AREA NHL ROUNDUP
The Predators shut out the Kings 3-0 in Los Angeles.  Filip Forsberg netted a pair of goals and Adam Wilsby put the game on ice with an empty-netter.  Juuse Saros made all 30 saves as Nashville extended its winning streak to five in-a-row.  Alex Laferriere rifled five shots on goal for LA, which has dropped back-to-back games. 

The Blues beat the Detroit Red Wings at home 3-2 last night.  Jimmy Snuggerud scored a goal and added an assist to take home first-star honors.  The Blues are back on the road tomorrow night to take on the Utah Mammoth. 

MLB MANAGER AWARDS
Major League Baseball yesterday announced the winners of the NL and AL Manager of the Year award.  Milwaukee Brewers skipper Pat Murphy made history after becoming the first to be named the National League Manager of the Year in three consecutive seasons.  Murphy finished ahead of Atlanta Braves manager Walt Weiss and Philadelphia Phillies bench boss Don Mattingly.  

Will Venable of the Chicago White Sox won the American League award.  Kevin Cash of the Tampa Bay Rays finished second and Chad Tracy of the Boston Red Sox was third.

AREA NFL ROUNDUP
The Buffalo Bills are adding a proven playmaker to their defense ahead of the NFL trade deadline, acquiring safety Amani Hooker from the Tennessee Titans for a second-round draft pick.  Buffalo is also picking up a fifth-round selection in the deal.  Hooker is leading the NFL with five interceptions so far this season. 

The San Francisco 49ers acquired veteran Keenan Allen from the Indianapolis Colts for a future sixth-round draft pick.  The 34-year-old is a six-time Pro Bowler who provides an instant veteran presence for a team who currently has six wideouts nursing short- and long-term injuries. 

The Atlanta Falcons signed Jake Moody off the Baltimore Ravens' practice squad and releasing Nick Folk.  Moody made a 53-yard field goal and an extra point for Baltimore this past Thursday in relief of the injured Tyler Loop.  The Falcons are parting with Folk after he missed field goals in back-to-back weeks, and five of 18 attempts this season. 

The Cincinnati Bengals' previously reported trade for defensive line help is now dead.  The team nixed its trade with the Philadelphia Eagles for edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie after learning the deal carried a hidden cost.  Cincinnati was poised to lose a third-round compensatory pick it won when Trey Hendrickson left in free agency on top of the sixth-round selection that was going to Philly.

Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh is addressing an incident involving wide receiver Calvin Ridley at Nashville International Airport over the weekend.  Saleh told reporters Monday that the situation appeared to be a very minor miscommunication and that law enforcement is handling the matter.  Few details have been released about what happened, and Saleh says the team plans to move forward with business as usual.

Scene I; Prelude, The Pied Piper and The Beavers

The 2nd Day of the 4th Moon, 1536 P.V.
Sapari

During the small hours, a messenger arrived in Sapari on horseback. The horse was somewhat foolish looking. It appeared to grin and had huge goofy teeth. The new harbour master, a young man named Billy Botwell who had been dispatched from Threnodyl after the strange disappearance of the old harbour master, tried not to stare. He considered staring rude but could not help glancing every now and then at the strange beast. He even smiled at the horse in a moment of awkwardness, and the horse grinned back, making him feel even more awkward. 

The situation worsened when a raven swooped down, landed on the quayside next to the horse, spilled in a heap of guts and bones and a red-headed pied piper, Chester, stepped out from the debris. 

Chester grew to his full height as the raven reassembled itself. Billy rubbed his eyes in disbelief, put the whole experience down to the Ashurrel leaf he was chewing, and spat it on the walkway.

‘That’s government property you’re soiling there!’ Chester pointed out with some force, squaring up to the poor little lad. The messenger riding the overfriendly horse, who was clad in purple and wore an eye patch, waved a hand at Chester,
‘Easy now, the lad is clearly new!’ 

The messenger smiled at the lad, the lad smiled back, and the messenger’s smile dropped,
‘Pick it up! Ya filthy landlubber!’ 
Billy dropped to his knees and scooped up the damp leaves, and not knowing what to do with them shoved them back into his mouth and gagged.

The messenger ignored the retching and got straight down to business. He informed the new harbour master that his name was Bigglesworth, Commodore Bigglesworth or Commodore Nicolas Bigglesworth, and stated that he had ridden through the night along the coast to relay an urgent message. Pirates were headed to Sapari. Not a single pirate ship, but several, a fleet in fact. An armada. The pirates, Nicolai-Bigglesworth claimed, were intending to steal wood from the shipyard. 

Billy did not think to ask where the message had emanated from or who had ordered its forwarding as he was still uneasy about the whole grinning horse and raven splatter debacle. 

Once the message had been relayed, and Bigglesworth’s first job of the day accomplished, Bigglesworth turned to Chester and explained his next job of the day,
‘The Immoless!’ He stated, without further explanation.
‘Neferaten,’ Chester replied. 

Chester then crouched down and the bone, guts and feathers of the same raven that had disturbed Billy, split apart, engulfed Chester and flew away at a speed only animals dosed with vampire blood could manage. Billy watched with his mouth agape, annoying Bigglesworth,
‘Well, boy! Don’t just stand staring, get the message out.’ 
Billy nodded and acted immediately. 

Bigglesworth made haste on Nicolas’s goofy vampiric horse, Zimba, along the quayside, bypassed the town and rode into the Dokeshi Carnival where he tethered the horse. He then summoned the guardians of Dokeshi, two demonic clown lovers, Scurra and Phylax to stand guard. Once the demons were in position, Bigglesworth crouched and allowed an albatross to absorb him and flew out to The Sombre.

The harbour master, who was a little disturbed by all the carry on, immediately sent word to the shipyard, and advised that they move the wood, via a caravan, to the village of Ashurrel that bordered Togaduine. This, Billy reasoned, was the only logical course of action as Ashurrel was far from port. He did not want the workers to enter Togaduine as, it was believed, a tyrant ruled the kingdom. A tyrant based in Corax Asylum. The labourers at the shipyard acted immediately.

Nonetheless, the new harbour master, being a bit of a jobsworth, decided to undertake every precaution. He declared that all ships should leave port and anchor together building an impenetrable wall on the horizon, whilst avoiding the local fishermen to prevent produce diminishment. It just so happened that the same harbour master had been gifted a cargo of anchors not a week before, from the brand ‘Ferromagnetic DeSilva,’ at least that is what the boxes said.

The ships formed their wall, and used the anchors to secure their positions, but it became apparent by late afternoon that there was no pirate armada, and the ships attempted to return to shore. However, somewhere there was a reversal of polarity in the magnetic anchors and the ships slammed together crunching the hulls, buckling the decks, and causing a huge mess in the ocean. The debris was formidable, and everyone forgot about the wood. 

When Billy finally dispatched a caravan to retrieve the wood they found it quite gone. Everyone was disgruntled, but before any investigation got underway Billy met an untimely death after a three ton anchor fell on his oversized head from a crane winch. The new harbour master soon became the old harbour master, and a harbour master from Ashurrel was sent to replace him, which was a little odd as Ashurrel had no proximity to the ocean. It was also a little odd that the new harbour master sported green locks, had eight eyes and called himself, ‘Rachnoc.’ The dock workers did not know what to make of Nicolai-Rachnoc and his excess of eyes, and rumours soon flew about that he was a loony recently escaped from Corax Asylum. The rumours were started by a dock labourer named Samson. The rumours stopped when Samson’s intestines accidentally released themselves from his body and wrapped around the drum of a dodgy capstan.

The Lord of Sapari wrote to Tepes to complain about the entire matter, and Tepes wrote to Theaten. Theaten forwarded his concerns to Nicolas by raven, and said letter was dumped, along with a few body parts, into the drains at Ashurrel. 

No one knew who was responsible for the Ferromagnetic anchors, but some recognised the horse. And there were rumours.

There were also rumours about Chester. Some claimed that the love god, who’s reputation preceded him, was a legend. Others believed he was Nicolas, or a cad, or a monster, and others still considered him to be an opportunistic postman. All rumours were, in fact, partially correct.

Chester was an infamous demon, infamous in Irkalla, and infamous in Corax Asylum, who Nicolas called the ‘The Pied Piper’ on account of the amount of beaver that followed him desperately trying to blow his massive flute. Nicolas was often jealous of Chester’s success with the ladies and put it down to his unusual appearance and impeccable taste. Chester was, in fact, a special Nicolai. He was the embodiment of Nicolas’s libido, his Evro, a walking dick and balls with the gift of the gab, and the skillset to match. 

During the snowy first moon of 1536 P.V., Chester had spent his time building up a following of sorts around Neferaten. He moved from village to village keeping the ladies of every occupation and class warm. He found that dressing as a postman opened doors, and legs, with very little explanation needed. His raven allowed him to move swiftly between villages and broaden his portfolio of conquests. He had intended to return to his ladies sooner, but Nicolas insisted that he spent the second and third moon with Allyra on account of Nicolas and the prolific scientist and strategist Nicolai-Webster developing the new plan, Plan BAT, Belua Alvearis Tyrannus.

This restriction on Chester’s movements caused a day of yowling, sulking and whining, but Nicolas flipped his two-headed coin for the job, and Chester lost. Chester considered Nicolas and Webster’s plans to be a waste of time as previous plans and procedures to alleviate the recurring problem troubling the Nicolai had failed. 

Webster called the problem Alveus Vacuus Problemus or AVP for short. 

Several plans had been executed over several centuries, and all failed with quite horrific consequences. Nicolas and Webster had really upped the ante during the previous five years, but their plans continued to backfire. Webster blamed Nicolas, and Nicolas blamed Webster. Chester did not care who blamed who, he cared that his balls were temporarily in a sling. Nonetheless, he did adhere to the new plan and spent two moons being the perfect boyfriend. Of course, he had been Allyra’s ‘perfect’ boyfriend for the past five years, but he diligently increased love-bombing and worrying Allyra with his fake sympathy, mesmerism and coercion to enhance that appearance for Nicolas’s sake. 

You see, Dear Reader, part of the problem worrying the Nicolai was that they did not have a queen, and part of the solution, Nicolas decided, involved taking a bride, and he had idealistic notions of how this should play out. These notions stemmed largely from his prolific reading of Carmilla Fanu’s dark romance novels. Nicolas somehow convinced himself that he was the dark handsome prince, protecting women from his own wrath. You could say that he misinterpreted the ideas behind the novels as he was conflicted in the realistic conveyance of the tropes. 

Nicolas understood that first he had to be the beast, and threatening, and then he had to also be the dark, morally grey, romantic hero redeemed by love. Unfortunately, Nicolas failed to realise that these novels were fiction, and that the heroes were not nearly as repulsive as he was. The repulsive beast came quite naturally to Nicolas, but the hero side not so much, and he had no interest in personal redemption of any sort. He also failed to correctly comprehend the order of the narrative functions. In practise this meant that most of the time his would-be brides were dead by Nicolas the Monster’s hand before Nicolas the Prince rocked up to save them.

Nicolas also misunderstood the word ‘no’ and interpreted it as the ‘princess’ being coy or shy, so when the potential bride reacted to his advances with some hostility, the beast became extraordinarily perturbed, and as such most of his plans failed spectacularly.

Now, Dear Reader, I have digressed a little from the prelude, or prologue, you may view it either way. This prelude focuses on the sufferings of Chester not the stupid ideas of Nicolas, so let us return to that. 

Nicolas was more than ready to descend upon Allyra, show her the beast and the prince, and generally make her life difficult until she fell in love with him. Since Nicolas had planned a busy day of annoying Allyra, or as Nicolas called it, ‘seducing the Immoless’ Chester was free to revisit the pussies of the ladies of Neferaten and secretly get Allyra back for hitting Nicolas with a metal rod.

Unfortunately for poor Chester, the ladies had moved on. 

Chester was quite happy to cheat and roam locating new conquests, and equally happy to dump any woman on a whim, but he did not take well to being the recipient of the same treatment.

He blamed the loose virtues of the women, not the manipulative natures of the men, for these atrocities and reacted with the wrath of a creature forlorn and broken-hearted by such cruel rejections.

The 2nd Day of the 4th Moon, 1536 P.V.
Neferaten

Chester took a detour to Corax, after his stopgap at Sapari, to change into his postman’s uniform, then flew directly to Tiye where hordes of beaver awaited his return. 

The beavers had arrived in Neferaten during the first moon of the year. They had followed Chester there, as beaver followed Chester everywhere, it was a burden he had to bear. The beaver remained in Tiye where they dropped logs and dug holes.

Chester had not gone to Tiye to meet the beavers. Nonetheless, he did lead them quickly to a watering hole by one of the bridges and blessed them by biting his own wrist and adding a few drops of blood to the water for the sake of their virility and fertility. That was what he claimed anyway.

Chester actually returned to Tiye to meet with the beautiful thesapien glassblower, Thalia. Thalia had fascinatingly bobbed, brown hair with thick streaks of ginger, which Chester approved of, and was able to examine in some detail as he spent most of his time with Thalia during the first moon, staring at the top of her head or watching himself fuck her in the glass. He liked the ginger in her hair as he liked women who reminded him of himself. Chester had spent the entire first week of the first moon with Thalia who demonstrated her prolific blowing skills on him. She also showed him the processes surrounding glass manufacturing. 

Although Nicolas had only offered Chester a day to hump his way through Neferaten on this occasion, a challenge Chester was more than capable of meeting, he had hoped to see Thalia’s head one last time before ending their courtship. 

Chester desperately wanted to surprise Thalia with his magnificent presence, and even considered railing her with his gloriously long tongue as a thank you. As such, our cat walked the circumference of the warehouse, climbed up the outer wall to the window and peered in. 

Chester liked to spy and stare, it was a common trait among the Immortalis who framed it as reasonably protective and caring behaviour as opposed to downright creepy and wrong. 

Thalia was busy blowing pipes, but there was no glass involved. Instead, she was blowing the pipes of the tanner and the cheesemaker, at the same time. It was one thing for Chester to romance three or four women at once, but for a woman to do it with multiple men seemed crude and outrageous. This, however, did not stop Chester staring, and one hand took a wander into his pants as the other paw clawed into the woodwork keeping him balanced. 

Passers-by opted not to look up as rumour had it that the sadist Nicolas masqueraded as a postman or a pied piper, also the people of The Deep were also used to postmen slipping more than letters into the women’s boxes.

Once all loads had been blown, Chester decided to pay Thalia a visit to confront her about her infidelity, even though they were not in a relationship. He waited until both men made their hasty departure, purchased a large jug of iced water to cool his temper from a street seller who wore a yellow and black robe and called himself Robert, then addressed his concerns with Thalia before her employees arrived. 

Thalia was unrepentant and annoyed, as if it was Chester’s fault that she was a hoe. During her angry rant, in which she attributed a comprehensive compendium of unpleasant nouns to Chester, Thalia inhaled so sharply and viciously that somehow molten glass just leapt from its crucible and into her mouth. The force of entry was so great that it spewed down her throat, followed closely by a glass jar of iced water. 

Chester rammed the glass in so hard that it cracked, tearing her lips, and mouth open. He pushed and rotated his hand continually until the whole container sat in shards in Thalia’s mouth and throat. The ice sizzled against the molten glass. Thalia’s eyes rolled back into white orbs as she tried to scream, but only steam came out. Then angry shards of glass desperately tried to escape their captivity by ripping through her throat. Her twitching body collapsed to the floor. More steam pumped out through the newly splayed orifices allowing Thalia to blow as much as she desired.

Chester was heartbroken. And hungry. His face elongated, his eyes narrowed and shone a ravenous emerald. As Thalia lay convulsing, Chester raised her skirt, pulled down her fine thong, and, after some exploration and tasting with his thick black tongue bit into her mound. She retched a few final attempts at breathing, then stilled. Chester took another bite, then another, swallowing the meat and blood as only a refined gentleman could. 

His thirst unexpectedly experienced additional satisfaction through the consumption of the thick blood provided by the moonly rationale for her offering only head to her suitors on that glorious day. This pleased Chester and he decided to have a quick goodbye fuck for luck. There was not much left to fuck, but he managed to locate the remains of two orifices that sat close together and this sufficed.

Chester bored of Tiye as soon as Thalia’s employees started showing up. The people were constant whingers. They complained about the loss of their chief glassblower, they complained about the beavers ‘upsetting the ecosystem,’ Chester didn’t even know what that meant, and they complained about the locusts that seemed to like Chester’s favourite aftershave. His aftershave was a bespoke and expensive number based on the erotic smell of rotting cabbages. The ladies seemed to like it too, or at least they met with an untimely demise if his taste in essences was brought into question. 

When Chester tired of the moaning, he changed course and travelled east to the village of Shepsut playing a merry tune from within his raven.

Some of the beavers remained in Tiye and some of the beavers followed.

The village of Shepsut operated both the grain stores and the laundry. Lilith did not care to do her own laundry, and despised the sight of washing lines, so all laundry in Shaenaten was sent to Shepsut. The Shepsutians made money, and Lilith did not have to look at the mess. This suited everyone. 

During his first moon in Neferaten, Chester had fallen in love with all the ladies of the grain store. On his return, and feeling irritably amorous, he discovered, after a little foreplay with three or four of his lovers, that a rather repulsive worm outbreak had occurred in places where worms ought not to be. 

Chester blamed the ink-eaters of the area who treated the granary as a brothel, and the brothel as another brothel, for the outbreak. The ink-eaters were renowned snobs, all of whom had families and worked in banking. 

The DeSilva Banks were operated by Pauley the Cheese and Nicolas’s public relations Nicolai, the black suited media mogul Monsieur Silas Gideon Alaric Bartholomew-Crispin (with a hyphen) Ledgerly. 

Ledgerly and Pauley had specifically noted on all contracts that employees were banned from having worms, lice, scabies or chlamydia. It seemed to Chester that the ink-eaters had failed to keep their end of the contract. He sent word via raven to Chives that the tertiary horde of Nicolai were to be dispatched to all branches and would take over immediately as managers given the obvious lapse in employee standards. 

Chives prepared the carriages. 

Ledgerly, who had just returned from Serphage with a printing job for Corax’s resident ghostwriter Nicolai-Bink ‘Binky’ McSnort regarding some inappropriate shenanigans by the coast, and Pauley the Cheese who had a day off from dosing the boars at the racetrack, went from town to town taking the third horde of Nicolai to the respective banks where they were immediately all declared manager. 

Pauley informed the staff of each branch, whilst he and Ledgerly had a little taste of the secretaries, that, in all branches, the new manger was called Mr Robert Robert. Nicolas had no issue in giving the Nicolai the same, or similar names. Several of the Nicolai were intentionally given variations of the name Nic, so that Nicolas could effectively praise himself when he praised them. 

The old bank managers were immediately declared insane and returned to Corax as a snack for the vampires. Each Robert Robert then directed the staff of each branch to change Theaten’s name on all paperwork to Lord Robert Robert of Robert. 

Chester could not let the matter of the worms rest. He was so hurt that the ladies he loved had tried to infect him that he introduced his favourite couple, Terry and Teresa Tapeworm to the grain stores.

In a moment of compassion, however, Chester decided to take his favourite laundry operator, the scrubber Mira, from Shepsut to the beautiful oasis of Seti, in the north, to save her virtue from the old and new worm outbreaks. He even allowed her to fly with him by raven. 

Some of the beavers followed with a haste only seen in creatures gifted with Immortalis or vampire blood.

Once at the oasis, Mira scrubbed Chester all over, polished and fiddled his flute, and swallowed every last note. Chester had trained her well and decided to train her further with a delicious threesome. On informing Mira of this idea, she seemed a little less enthusiastic about Chester, but he was determined to pursue the matter and scuttled off to find some nice women open to joining in.

text:
Honda Canada to retool Alliston, Ont., plant to expand hybrid production
Story by Sammy Hudes • 19h • 2 min read
The Canadian Press

Honda Canada says it will retool its manufacturing facilities in Alliston, Ont., to expand production of hybrid-electric and gasoline-powered vehicles.

The Japanese automaker announced Monday it is partnering with the federal and provincial governments to fund plant upgrades, including the reintroduction of engine manufacturing, with an initial $166 million investment.

It said that funding is part of a broader $867-million commitment that will enhance quality, efficiency and manufacturing flexibility. Of that total, the federal government said it will provide $313 million, while the Ontario government is kicking in $156 million.

"This renewed investment reinforces Canada's critical role in Honda's North American growth and hybrid-electric vehicle strategy and helps position our operations for long-term competitiveness and future opportunities," said Honda Canada president and CEO Dave Jamieson in a news release.

The funding will ensure Honda can maintain its workforce of 4,000 Canadian employees across two facilities at the Alliston plant, while supporting its Canadian auto production volumes.

The company said it will also strengthen the Alliston plant's operations to help meet growing customer demand for hybrid-electric vehicles in North America.

"This investment will strengthen our automotive supply chains, support thousands of well-paying jobs in Ontario and across the country, and help build a strong Canadian auto sector where workers build the cars of the future," said Industry Minister Mélanie Joly in a statement.

Ontario Premier Doug Ford called the investment "a clear vote of confidence in the 4,000 world-class Ontario auto workers employed at the plant."

"In the face of tariffs and economic uncertainty, we’re delivering on our plan to make Ontario more competitive so we can protect workers and attract job-creating investments like this one from around the globe," he said in a statement on social media.

In May, Honda announced plans to introduce 15 new Honda and Acura hybrid models globally by 2030, with North America expected to be the primary market for many of those vehicles.

The automaker said it is investing across its manufacturing network in Canada, Ohio, Alabama and Georgia to support that strategy.

That same month, the company indefinitely suspended its plans for a $15-billion Canadian electric vehicle complex in response to dwindling demand.

Announced in 2024, Honda's EV project would have included a vehicle assembly plant as well as battery production facilities. It had said that new EV plant could create 1,000 incremental manufacturing jobs in Alliston.

It was set to receive upwards of $5 billion in federal and Ontario funding, however no money had yet been transferred.

The decision to pause those plans did not affect current employment or production levels at the Alliston plant.

More than 400,000 vehicles were produced at the site last year. Honda is Canada's second largest auto manufacturer by volume.

Tank Dell caught a touchdown yesterday for the first time in 687 days, and the last one he caught is the play that dislocated his knee.

That was the 21st of December, 2024, in Kansas City. C.J. Stroud threw it to him and he took it 30 yards and scored.

Then he collided with Jared Wayne.

Wayne is a receiver on his own team. It was the second NFL game of his life. Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle later wrote that it was a freak accident and that nobody was at fault.

Dell's knee came out of its socket and he tore multiple ligaments in it. They carted him off and kept him in a Kansas City hospital overnight.

He did not play a single game in 2025.

Wayne got blamed for it online. He cried for days and went and got counseling. His teammates and his coaches told him it was not his fault and he could not make himself believe them.

He wrote to Dell.

Dell did not see the message for days, because he was dealing with his own grief.

"I told him, 'Ease up, yo, it's football,' and I know it was a genuine mistake."

"Man, it's good. God got me. Ease up, man. Go play, go have fun, play football."

"It was cool. There are no hard feelings. That's my brother, so we're cool."

He has said the anger he felt was about the knee and never about Wayne.

"God wants you to forgive."

"Who would I be if I didn't forgive him?"

They joke with each other now.

He is listed at 5 foot 10 and 165 pounds, and he measured 5 foot 8 and three eighths at the Combine.

He grew up in Daytona Beach and went to Mainland High School there. He had committed to Florida International out of high school.

He started at Alabama A&M, left for a junior college in Kansas, and finished at Houston, where in 2022 he led the entire country in receiving yards and in receiving touchdowns. The Texans took him in the third round, 69th overall.

He broke the fibula in his left leg in the 13th game of his rookie year, against Denver, and had surgery the next day. He had 47 catches and seven touchdowns before that happened, and 51 catches and 667 yards in 2024 before the night in Kansas City.

He opened this season on injured reserve. Houston activated him on the 24th of October, and his first catch back went 43 yards, 673 days after his previous one.

Wayne had never talked about any of it in public until August, when he told Alexander what he thought was coming.

"Whenever he catches that first one, I might shed a tear."

YESTERDAY at SoFi Stadium, with Houston ahead 10 to 9 in the second quarter, Stroud went deep right. Dell caught it and ran it 63 yards.

The Texans won 44 to 22.

One of Kansas’ premier baseball talents is officially taking the next step in his career. Girard standout Kam Smith signed with the University of Arkansas, making his commitment to one of the top programs in college baseball official.

Smith is coming off a historic junior season, helping lead Girard to its first-ever Class 3A state baseball championship. He was named the Sports in Kansas 2026 Class 3A Pitcher of the Year after recording 112 strikeouts in 64.1 innings with a 0.32 ERA. The 6-foot-3 right-hander has also seen his fastball reach 92 MPH. He was also the Sports in Kansas All-Classes Pitcher of the Year and a Top 9 all classes selection. He was also the 3A pitcher of the year from SIK as a sophomore in 2025 and is already a three time all state pick with a season left. 

Baseball is more than just a sport in the Smith family. It’s a tradition that spans generations in Girard. His father, Dan Smith Jr., was a standout pitcher at Girard High School, earning 1993 Kansas Gatorade Player of the Year honors as a senior before being selected 199th overall by the Texas Rangers in the 1993 MLB Draft. Dan went on to play in the major leagues.

His uncle, Dustin Smith, also continued the baseball tradition as a former minor league player and professional scout. His late grandfather, Dan Smith Sr., was a respected and well-connected baseball coach at Girard, helping build the program and its tradition.

The athletic talent extends throughout the family as well, with Kam’s sister competing in the triple jump at Pittsburg State University.

Now, Kam gets the opportunity to add another chapter to the family legacy. After establishing himself as one of the top pitching prospects in the 2027 class and helping deliver a historic state championship to his hometown, he’ll take his talents to Fayetteville and compete in the SEC with the Arkansas Razorbacks.

A special day for Kam, his family and the entire Girard community. Cameron Birney was in town to cover the event and we will hear from Smith later. #sportsinkansas

Republicans won every statewide race in Arkansas last Tuesday. Don't let anyone in Little Rock tell you it was a good night.

I spent the last week going through every precinct result in this state back to 2012, plus the campaign finance reports. The numbers tell a story our party leadership would rather you not hear.

Governor Sanders won by 17 points. Four years ago she won by 28. Every statewide and congressional race with a Democrat on the ballot lost 12 to 24 points of margin. 73 of our 75 counties moved toward the Democrat. The 2nd Congressional District held by 4,356 votes.

Democrats flipped 11 State House seats and a State Senate seat. The House went from 81-19 to 70-30.

Here is the part that matters most. Democrats did not surge. Their nominee for governor gained 22,178 votes over 2022. Governor Sanders lost 94,702. Republican voters did not switch sides. The numbers say most of them stayed home or voted Libertarian.

Look at the races with no Democrat at all. For Lieutenant Governor and Land Commissioner, about 300,000 Arkansans, 36 percent of the vote, chose the Libertarian over the Republican nominee. That is not a Democratic wave. That is Republican voters telling us they have lost confidence in the people running our party.

And it was not money. In the 12 legislative seats we lost, Republicans outspent Democrats in 10. $1.36 million to $408,000. In Senate District 13 alone, $619,000 on our side and $67,000 on theirs. We lost it anyway.

You cannot buy back trust you have already spent.

That is a stewardship problem, and it sits at the top. It sits with the Governor, who backed Chairman Joseph Wood for another term, and with the party leadership under Chairman Wood and Executive Director Drew Martin. In the Army, when a unit loses ground, the commander answers for it. No one in this chain of command has answered for anything.

If nothing changes, 2028 will be worse, and the data already shows where. Seven Republican House seats were within 15 points for governor and Democrats did not even field a candidate. House District 18 was within 3. Two Republicans already hold seats that voted Democrat for governor. The 2nd District is a coin flip. Senate Districts 17 and 33 are next.

Democrats will find candidates for those seats. The only question is whether we find our way back first.

As long as Chairman Wood and Drew Martin stay in place, I expect the slide to continue. We need fewer Cody Smiths in this party and more men and women of character who keep their word and answer for their results.

The voters who walked away are not lost. They are waiting for a party worth coming home to.

text:
$WGS Q3 2026 earnings: GeneDx collects higher payments per test, but cuts growth targets

GeneDx, a genetics lab that sequences DNA to diagnose rare diseases, is getting paid more per test while its test volume slows down. Third-quarter sales grew 5% from a year ago to $123 million as average payment per core exome and genome test rose 5% from last quarter, lifting profit excluding one-offs to $9 million. However, completed core test volume missed the company's target, forcing chief executive Katherine Stueland to cut full-year growth floors for core volume and core revenue for a second time this year.

• Exome and genome revenue: $𝟏𝟏𝟎.𝟒𝐌 (+12% from a year ago)
• Average revenue per exome/genome test: ~$𝟑,𝟒𝟑𝟎 (+5% from last quarter (plan: ~$3,300))
• Net profit, excluding one-offs: $𝟖.𝟔𝐌 (plan: ~$2.0M (GAAP net loss: -$12.3M))
• Full-year exome/genome revenue outlook: 𝐂𝐮𝐭 𝐭𝐨 ≥𝟏𝟕% (prior: ≥20% (total revenue held at $475–490M))

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: ⚪ Neutral

The story is unchanged because higher reimbursement per test and lower full-year volume targets cancelled each other out. Average revenue per core test climbed to about $3,430 and the fourth-quarter plan points to $3,507 by our math, easing the main worry that insurance payments were stuck. The bad news: cutting the full-year core revenue growth floor to 17% confirms that the earlier 20% target was out of reach, and free cash flow burn reached $16 million in the quarter.

The question now is whether rising payment per test comes from insurers paying new whole genome claims or from one-time accounting adjustments to older bills. If new insurance policies are paying out, fourth-quarter collections will turn cash flow positive; if accounting adjustments drove the gain, unpaid bills will keep climbing. The quarterly filing's revenue footnote and fourth-quarter cash flow will settle it.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐀𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞 𝐏𝐚𝐲𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐏𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐓𝐮𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐝 𝐔𝐩𝐰𝐚𝐫𝐝
GeneDx sequences a patient's exome (the protein-coding part of DNA) or whole genome to diagnose rare diseases. Average revenue per test fell earlier this year because orders shifted toward whole genome tests, which insurers paid less often. This quarter, average revenue per exome and genome test rose 5.5% from last quarter to $3,436 by our math, beating the $3,300 plan.

The genetics lab reported "Q3 ARR up 5% sequentially to ~$3,430" and noted "No material changes to underlying average contracted rates this quarter" in its presentation. Because contract prices stayed the same, the higher average payment came from collecting on more claims and steering doctors toward tests with better insurance coverage. By our math, the fourth-quarter outlook points to $3,507 per test.

What to watch: the exact outpatient collection rate and prior-period billing adjustments in the quarterly filing. A rise above the 32% collection rate from the first half, without a large one-time billing true-up, would prove that newly added insurance policies are paying out.

🟢 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐬𝐬 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐓𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭𝐬 𝐌𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐝 𝐔𝐩
Better payment per test and earlier staff cuts lifted margins past the company's plan. Gross margin excluding one-offs (revenue left after the cost of running the lab) rose to 71.6% from 70.4% last quarter, beating the 70% target. Selling and administrative overhead excluding one-offs fell by 3.4 percentage points of revenue from last quarter to 52.0%, though it remains 7.6 points higher than a year ago.

Net profit excluding one-offs reached $8.6 million against a $2 million plan, and management raised the full-year profit target to about $12 million. However, new accounting adjustments flattered that result. The rare-disease specialist still lost $12.3 million under standard accounting, and its adjusted profit now strips out $1.8 million of net interest expense, $1.2 million of vacant lease costs, and "third party advisor fees related to our Revenue Cycle Transformation".

What to watch: operating profit under standard accounting in the fourth quarter. Shrinking the gap between standard losses and adjusted profit will show whether cost discipline is outrunning consulting and interest bills.

🟢 𝐏𝐚𝐲𝐞𝐫 𝐂𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐎𝐫𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐓𝐨𝐨𝐥𝐬 𝐊𝐞𝐞𝐩 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠
The company is trying to win orders from general pediatricians while getting more state Medicaid programmes to pay for whole genome sequencing. This quarter, Arkansas and Utah Medicaid added coverage for whole genome tests, bringing the total to 25 states. Management also hired Nicole Maassen as Chief Patient Access Officer for "translating positive coverage policies into timely access for children who need testing".

On the product side, the diagnostics provider rolled out "simplified test reports, easy ordering, and report guides" for doctors and launched "long-read whole genome sequencing" to defend its share in advanced testing. It also opened an online service where families of children with developmental delays or epilepsy can connect with doctors to order exome tests "without requiring traditional in-person visits".

What to watch: test volume from the "Dedicated team of ~50 sales reps expected to drive impact by the end of 2026 and into 2027". Because selling overhead is up 7.6 percentage points of revenue from a year ago, those reps must start bringing in orders in the fourth quarter to justify their cost.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐂𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡 𝐓𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭𝐬 𝐂𝐮𝐭 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐚 𝐒𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐝 𝐓𝐢𝐦𝐞
"Our Q3 results reflect profitable execution in a growing market, as we translate the rising demand for exome and genome testing into durable revenue growth," chief executive Katherine Stueland said. Yet for the second time this year, the testing company cut its full-year growth targets for exome and genome tests after third-quarter completed test volume missed its own plan.

• Q3 exome and genome test volume: 32,134 tests (up 25% from a year ago), missing the 33,200 target
• Full-year exome and genome volume growth outlook: cut to at least 28%, down from 30% last quarter and 33–35% at the start of the year
• Full-year exome and genome revenue growth outlook: cut to at least 17%, down from 20% last quarter and 33–35% at the start of the year
• Full-year total revenue implied by Q4 outlook: $474.8 million by our math, just below the reiterated $475–490 million range

The company noted that accessions (incoming test samples) grew 28% from a year ago, three points faster than completed test results. Even so, the fourth-quarter target of $121 million in exome and genome sales fell $9.5 million short of what the old 20% full-year floor required by our math, proving that third-quarter payment gains could not make up for slower test counts.

What to watch: whether fourth-quarter exome and genome volume clears 34,500 tests. Another shortfall would show that stricter insurance checks prior to testing are slowing down doctors' orders.

🔴🔴 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐁𝐮𝐫𝐧 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐮𝐞𝐬 𝐖𝐡𝐢𝐥𝐞 𝐃𝐞𝐛𝐭 𝐓𝐫𝐢𝐩𝐥𝐞𝐬
Higher adjusted profit has not yet turned into cash in the bank. By our math from the nine-month cash flow statement, the Maryland-based company used $10.6 million of cash in its operations during the third quarter and spent $5.2 million on lab equipment and software, burning $15.8 million of free cash flow. Over the first nine months of 2026, free cash flow burn reached $93.8 million.

Cash stayed tied up in unpaid bills: accounts receivable (money owed by insurers and patients) climbed to $92.1 million, up 23.9% since December while third-quarter revenue grew 5.4% from a year ago. To keep $171.1 million of total cash on hand after the August Blackstone loan expansion, the business tripled its long-term debt from $48.2 million at year-end to $146.2 million, cutting net cash to $24.9 million by our math.

What to watch: fourth-quarter operating cash flow, which finance chief Kevin Feeley previously committed would turn positive. Continuing to burn cash while carrying $146.2 million of debt would pressure the balance sheet in 2027.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
Four standing concerns could not be read from the earnings release and slide deck because the company discloses them on the conference call or in its quarterly filing.

• Outpatient genome collection rate and genome share of test volume: slide 19 names both as key metrics without printing clear third-quarter percentages; the call transcript will show whether collections moved off 32% and whether genome mix stayed near 30%.
• Prior-period billing estimate changes: in the second quarter, $7.3 million of revenue came from upward adjustments to older quarters' bills; the quarterly filing's revenue footnote will show how much of the third-quarter payment jump came from similar true-ups.
• Lab supply costs: whole genome tests cost nearly twice as much to run as exome tests, with cost relief previously pushed to 2027; the call will show if supplier pricing changed.
• Shareholder lawsuits over Fabric Genomics: two class-action suits filed in June and July over the impaired software acquisition were not mentioned in the release; the quarterly filing's legal footnote will carry any update.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐩𝐚𝐧𝐞𝐥 𝐭𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟗.𝟕 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Sales of older, narrower gene panel tests fell 33.6% from a year ago and 16.4% from last quarter as doctors switched to full exome and genome tests. Panel test volume dropped 23.1% from a year ago to 26,524 tests, holding total company revenue growth to 5.4% despite 11.6% growth in exome and genome sales.

𝐀𝐜𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐢𝐯𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟗𝟐.𝟏 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Uncollected customer and insurer bills rose 51.2% from a year ago and 23.9% from the end of 2025, outpacing third-quarter revenue growth of 5.4%. Because GeneDx books revenue based on expected collections before insurers actually pay, rising receivables drained $18.0 million of operating cash over the first nine months.

𝐃𝐢𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭, 𝐞𝐱𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐧𝐞-𝐨𝐟𝐟𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟑𝟎.𝟕𝟔 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
The diluted share count used for profit excluding one-offs rose 2.0% from a year ago and 2.0% from last quarter. The increase reflects employee stock compensation and the August private sale of shares to Blackstone alongside the expanded term loan.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞: $𝟒𝟕𝟓–𝟒𝟗𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
🠆 unchanged from $475–490 million
Unchanged. The full-year target still calls for 12.9% growth at the middle of the range, after management cut it by $65 million in the first quarter. However, by our math, nine-month sales of $339.8 million plus the new $135 million fourth-quarter target add up to $474.8 million, sitting right at the bottom edge of the annual range.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐄𝐱𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐯𝐨𝐥𝐮𝐦𝐞 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡: 𝐀𝐭 𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐭 𝟐𝟖% 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡  ⇘ decelerating
🠇 cut from At least 30% growth
Cut. Management lowered the full-year volume growth floor by 2 percentage points after third-quarter volume missed its target. In Sumerian cosmology
The Sumerian god Enki (Ea in the Akkadian language) was believed to have keen eyes and appeared out of the abzû since before human beings were created. His wife Damgalnuna, his mother Nammu, his advisor Isimud and a variety of subservient creatures, such as the gatekeeper Lahmu, also lived in the abzû.[4][5][6][7][8]

Abzû (apsû) is depicted as a deity[9] only in the Babylonian creation epic, the Enūma Eliš, taken from the library of Assurbanipal (c. 630 BCE) but which is about 500 years older. In this story, he was a primal being made of fresh water and a lover to another primal deity, Tiamat, a creature of salt water. The Enūma Eliš begins:

"When above the heavens (e-nu-ma e-liš) did not yet exist
nor the earth below,
Apsû the freshwater ocean was there, the first, the begetter,
and Tiamat, the saltwater sea, she who bore them all;
they were still mixing their waters,
and no pasture land had yet been formed,
nor even a reed marsh."
The act of procreation led to the birth of the younger gods: Enki, Enlil, and Anu. Anchored in the Tablet of Destinies, they founded an organisation to make Mesopotamia fertile through agriculture, but got into a dispute and consequently created the first humans as labour slaves, to peacefully resolve the conflict. The humans multiplied en masse and disturbed the gods around Enlil and Anu with their noise, so that they wanted to use the cosmic freshwater ocean to trigger the great flood and destroy the humans (cf. Athrahasis epic). Enraged by the devastation of earth, Tiamat gave birth to monsters whose bodies she filled with "poison instead of blood" and waged war against her traitorous children. Only Marduk, the founder of Babylon, was able to kill Tiamat and mould the final constitution of heaven and earth from her corpse.

ELECTION WATCH 2026 — FEDERAL / STATE

November 11, 2026 | Strategic Assessment

ELECTION INTEGRITY

Two immediate priorities before January 2027:

1. Mandatory Election Audits: Every federal and state election race must undergo a transparent, independent post-election audit examining vote accuracy, ballot integrity, chain of custody, voter eligibility, and potential fraud. Any credible evidence of wrongdoing must be investigated and prosecuted where warranted.

2. PASS THE SAVE AMERICA ACT: Congress must pass the SAVE America Act and send it to President Trump for signature before Democrats assume control of Congress on January 3, 2027.

ACCOUNTABILITY: Election Watch will identify which congressional leaders support these reforms, who obstructs them, and what legislative opportunities Republicans allow to expire.

Election integrity cannot be left to political promises. It requires enforceable law, independent verification, and accountability.

EXECUTIVE ASSESSMENT — THE COST OF REPUBLICAN INACTION

Republicans are approaching the January transfer of power with a rapidly closing opportunity to enact durable institutional reforms. Yet several Republican governors and legislative leaders are declining to exercise their remaining authority.

The central question:

Why are Republican leaders declining to enact lawful, durable institutional reforms while they still possess the power to do so, and which specific opportunities will become unavailable in January?

A principal legislative priority should be preventing a repeat of COVID-era government overreach by restricting the extraordinary emergency powers exercised by governors.

The objective is not to eliminate emergency response capabilities. It is to prevent temporary emergency authority from becoming prolonged government by executive decree.

The distinction is between political unwillingness and genuine legislative constraints.

1. TEXAS — THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL OPPORTUNITY

STATUS: SPECIAL SESSION REQUESTED — NOT CONVENED

Following the November 3 election of Democrat Gina Hinojosa, Republican Rep. Brian Harrison called on outgoing Gov. Greg Abbott to convene an immediate special session restricting gubernatorial emergency powers.

Harrison’s previously introduced HB 911 provides a legislative framework:

• Prohibit unilateral suspension or modification of statutes.

• Require legislative approval to extend disaster declarations beyond 30 days.

• Automatically expire certain emergency orders affecting constitutional rights unless lawmakers extend them.

• Prohibit reissuance of rejected or expired orders, subject to limited exceptions.

• Require narrowly tailored restrictions and expedited judicial review.

These are protections that should apply regardless of political affiliation.

Texas Government Code §§418.012–418.016 currently authorizes executive orders with the force of law, gubernatorial renewal of disaster declarations, and suspension of certain regulatory requirements.

LEGISLATIVE OBSTACLE: Republicans hold 88 Texas House seats and 19 Senate seats. A two-thirds quorum requires 100 representatives and 21 senators. Legislation taking effect immediately also requires two-thirds approval in each chamber.

Therefore, Abbott can call a session, but Republicans cannot independently guarantee its success.

ASSESSMENT: No verified special-session proclamation. Abbott has not publicly committed to Harrison’s proposal. The political decision to convene the Legislature and the constitutional votes needed to enact immediate protections are separate questions.

Once Democrats assume the governorship and House majority in January, this opportunity fundamentally changes.

2. IOWA — AN EXAMPLE OF LEGISLATIVE ACTION

STATUS: EMERGENCY-POWER REFORMS ALREADY ENACTED

Republican Gov. Kim Reynolds signed HF 2694 on June 2, effective July 1.

The legislation restricts gubernatorial emergency authority involving religious worship, business closures during public-health disasters, vaccination mandates, private residences, and unilateral election-law changes.

Importantly, it does not establish a general requirement for legislative approval of every 30-day emergency extension.

Following Democrat Rob Sand’s election as governor, Republican House Speaker Pat Grassley stated November 6 that another special session was not under consideration.

ASSESSMENT: Iowa demonstrates that meaningful institutional protections can be enacted before an election. Republican inaction after November should not be confused with a failure to legislate previously.

3. GEORGIA — A DELIBERATE REFUSAL

STATUS: SPECIAL SESSION REJECTED

On November 4, outgoing Republican Gov. Brian Kemp rejected calls for a special legislative session to limit incoming Democratic Gov. Keisha Lance Bottoms’ authority or redraw legislative districts.

Kemp cited respect for the election outcome.

Democrats have also secured control of Georgia’s House. Republicans retain the Senate.

Georgia lawmakers could compel a special session only with three-fifths certification from both chambers, a threshold Republicans cannot independently satisfy.

ASSESSMENT: Kemp’s refusal is a documented political decision, distinct from the separate constitutional limitations on lawmakers convening themselves.

No new reversal of that position has been verified.

4. CONGRESS — THE JANUARY 3 DEADLINE

STATUS: LEGISLATIVE PUSH ORGANIZING — NOMINATIONS ADVANCING

Republicans lose both congressional majorities on January 3, 2027.

Sen. Bernie Moreno has advocated remaining in Washington through December 31 to enact Republican priorities, including a budget reconciliation package.

On November 10, Senate Majority Leader John Thune committed to extending the legislative calendar, advancing nominations, funding the government, and pursuing additional legislation.

The Senate voted 62–21 to proceed to H.R. 2347, the vehicle for permitting reform. This was procedural action, not final passage.

The Senate Judiciary Committee separately advanced four district-court nominees:

• Daniel Ballou — Kentucky, 12–10.

• Richard Bennett — Texas, 12–10.

• Courtney Coker — Texas, 12–10.

• Kyle Reardon — Alaska, 16–6.

These nominees await full Senate confirmation.

ASSESSMENT: Republicans are demonstrating greater urgency on lifetime judicial appointments than on completing a comprehensive institutional reform package.

Judicial confirmations generally require a simple Senate majority. Ordinary legislation can face a 60-vote cloture threshold, while reconciliation is restricted principally to qualifying budgetary provisions.

Those constraints are genuine, but they do not explain every instance of legislative inaction.

5. REFORMS THAT SHOULD BE EVALUATED BEFORE JANUARY

The emergency-powers question deserves particular attention.

A durable statutory framework should establish:

1. A 30-day limit on unilateral emergency declarations, followed by affirmative legislative approval.
2. Automatic legislative review of prolonged emergencies.
3. Narrow restrictions on business, school, and religious closures, preserving necessary immediate responses.
4. Protections for medical consent, private residences, constitutional liberties, and due process.
5. Restrictions on unilateral executive modification of election laws.
6. Expedited judicial review.
7. Automatic expiration of emergency orders lacking renewed legal authority.

These safeguards must be evaluated against constitutional requirements and genuine emergency-response needs.

The objective is to ensure that another public-health emergency / contrived emergency cannot become an indefinite suspension of ordinary representative government.

STRATEGIC CONCLUSION — POLITICAL WILL VS. INSTITUTIONAL LIMITATIONS

Texas has a specific legislative proposal but no convened session.

Iowa enacted significant restrictions before the election.

Georgia’s governor expressly declined to convene lawmakers.

Congressional Republicans are accelerating judicial appointments while their broader legislative agenda remains uncertain.

The remaining question is not merely what Republicans say they support.

It is what they have the lawful power and votes to enact, what they actually attempt, and what they allow to become impossible after January.

A constitutional limitation is a legitimate obstacle. A decision not to introduce legislation, convene a session, schedule a vote, or use available legislative procedures is a different matter.

BOTTOM LINE: Republicans should be judged by enacted institutional protections, not declarations of intent.

Once authority changes hands in January, political explanations will not recover opportunities that were allowed to expire.

The most interesting thing about Jon Ossoff becoming the 2028 favourite isn't his age, his fundraising or even that Georgia result. It's the particular Democratic problem he seems capable of solving.

Democrats need someone who can make the party feel younger and more combative without making it feel more ideological. Ossoff has the ability to do both.

Donald Trump won Georgia in 2024. Two years later, Ossoff won his Senate race with roughly 59% of the vote. More importantly, he improved on Kamala Harris's 2024 performance in every county in the state and almost every precinct. He also flipped a dozen counties Trump had carried.

That matters because this wasn't simply a case of Democrats turning out more Democrats. Ossoff won roughly two-thirds of independents and made substantial gains with white voters, while still performing strongly with younger voters and the Democratic base.

That starts to look like the coalition Democrats need to take the White House in 2028. Not a candidate who wins the argument inside the party. A candidate who expands the party.

Ossoff is interesting because he combines things Democrats usually struggle to find in the same politician. 
- He can attack Trump hard without sounding permanently online. 
- He can talk about corruption, healthcare and cost of living in language that travels beyond the progressive base.
- He is young enough to embody generational change without asking voters to sign up to an ideological revolution.
- And he has spent six years building a fairly conventional Senate record rather than becoming defined by one faction of the party.

What Ossoff offers that is different to other potential candiates is generational change without an ideological revolution.

He will be 41 in 2028. That matters less because America needs a young president and more because the Democratic Party badly needs to look like it has moved into a new political era.

Biden represented restoration. Harris represented continuity with that administration. The next Democratic nominee may need to represent a break.

But the danger is that “break” becomes shorthand for moving sharply left or fighting another internal ideological battle. Ossoff offers a cleaner version of change. Different generation. Different communication style. Different energy. But without asking swing voters to accept a dramatically different Democratic Party.

2026 was a good Democratic year. His Republican opponent had serious weaknesses. Winning a Senate race in Georgia is not the same as surviving a presidential primary. But presidential candidates usually become serious because they appear to solve a problem their party has not yet worked out how to solve.

For Democrats, that problem may be becoming clearer. How do you fight Trumpism without making Trump the centre of everything? How do you recover independents without depressing the base? How do you look like change without frightening swing voters? 
How do you bring younger voters back without sounding like politics designed exclusively for younger voters?

Ossoff has just run a campaign that appears to have done all four. It may be an early signal that Democrats are beginning to work out what they want their next candidate to look like.

Not a return. Not a revolution. A reset.
